current.text: Peyton Watson has left Denver. Johnson is a projected starter at forward next to Aaron Gordon and Nikola Jokic.
With Watson gone, experts say Johnson should have to start, and that the change helps his outlook.
Denver is short on spacing after losing Tim Hardaway Jr. and needs shooters who will shoot off Jokic.
One expert expects Denver to trade Johnson to get under the second apron, before the trade deadline.
Experts expect a bounce-back season and say he could be clearly better than last season.
A top 120 season is possible. If his usage rises from 15 to 18 percent he could be top 100, and the best case is about top 90.
Experts in mock drafts see him as good value as a last-round pick, around picks 123 to 144.

Denver plays 43 games through March 28, one fewer than the most any team plays, and has only 14 back-to-backs, one of the lowest totals in the league. It also gets one of only three five-game weeks this season.

durable.text: He is an elite shooter who does little else. He gives threes, a good free throw percentage and a solid field goal percentage.
He is 30 and has a history of ankle and hip injuries. He has played 58 or fewer games in each of the last three seasons.

note: He ranks 148 on Yahoo and 140 on ESPN, right at the edge of our 144-player draft. Both sites price him at about 1 USD, and he went for 4 USD in our league last season, so he is a 1 to 2 USD last pick for threes, FT% and low turnovers that fits any build. Early in the season, check whether his usage rises toward 18 percent as a starter and whether Denver trades him, because a trade could shrink his role.
